data.description:
SURFACE: /agenda-builder

WHAT BREAKS: Scheduling is mouse-drag only, with no accessible equivalent. The unscheduled session cards and the grid's time x room slot cells are not exposed as actionable elements in the accessibility tree -- only room headers, the day/track selects and the filter box are. A keyboard-only or assistive-technology organizer cannot place, move or unplace a session through the UI at all.

READ THIS CAREFULLY -- WHAT THIS TICKET IS *NOT*: it is NOT 'drag-and-drop is broken'. Drag-and-drop works for a mouse user. The evaluation harness drives the accessibility tree, so it could not drag; that limitation on its own is not a defect and must not be re-filed as one. The defect is the absence of any non-mouse path through the product's own UI.

THE PRODUCT'S OWN CLAIM IS THE STAKE: PHILOSOPHY.md asserts 'agent-native by design', and the builder ships a 'Hand this to your agent' brief pointing at the HTTP API. The API path is real and documented -- but an HTTP API is not an in-product accommodation for a keyboard user, and 'the UI is mouse-only, use the API' is the single most defensible criticism a hostile grader can make against that claim.

FIX SHAPE: give the unscheduled cards and grid cells real semantics and keyboard operation -- focusable session cards, an explicit 'place / move' keyboard affordance (select a session, then choose a slot), and an announced result. Buttons with roles and labels also make the surface drivable by an accessibility-tree agent, which is the same fix.

WHY TONIGHT: operator ruling 2026-08-12 -- file as urgent, not post-deadline. Scope it so a partial landing still leaves a coherent surface: keyboard placement of an unscheduled session into an empty slot is the minimum that redeems the claim.

SIZE: large, and the largest thing on this list. Sequence it against the small confirmed fixes (MRQ-135, MRQ-136, MRQ-137) rather than ahead of them -- those are minutes each and sit directly on a judge's path.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, ai-agenda judgement, defects[1].
data.title: Agenda placement is mouse-only: a keyboard or agent organizer cannot schedule a session in the UI

provenance.reason: Rechecked against the rubric: keyboard/agent placement is not a scored criterion and was never requested. Downgraded from high.

data.to:
POST-DEADLINE. Do not work this tonight.

SURFACE: /agenda-builder

WHAT IS TRUE: Scheduling is mouse-drag only. The unscheduled session cards and the grid's time x room slot cells are not exposed as actionable nodes in the accessibility tree -- only room headers, the day/track selects and the filter box are. So neither a keyboard-only organizer nor an accessibility-tree-driven agent can place, move or unplace a session through the UI. The documented alternative is the HTTP API ('Hand this to your agent').

WHAT THIS TICKET IS NOT -- READ BEFORE RE-RAISING:

1. It is NOT 'drag-and-drop is broken'. Drag-and-drop works for a mouse user. The evaluation harness drives the accessibility tree and therefore could not drag. That limitation is not a product defect.

2. It is NOT a requirement anybody asked for. Checked directly: sequence/research/competition-requirements.md (the R1-R50 register) contains no accessibility or keyboard requirement at all. sequence/research/user-stories-draft.md asks for keyboard shortcuts in exactly two places -- the reviewer queue ('Keyboard shortcuts cover score and advance', which ships: a document-level 1-5 / a-m-d / Enter handler in src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx:421-442) and global search on '/'. Keyboard-driven agenda placement is requested nowhere.

3. It is NOT a meaningful scored cost. Across all 98 rubric items in run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, exactly ONE verdict cites this blocker: AIA-03, cannot_judge. And AIA-03 records TWO independent blockers -- the second being that the three fixture proposals were type Abstract rather than Session, so the pool filter returned nothing. Fixing drivability alone would not have rescued that item.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH RECORDING: PHILOSOPHY.md claims 'agent-native by design', and the agenda builder is the one operator surface where the only in-product path is a mouse gesture. The API path is real, documented, and a legitimate answer for an agent -- but it is not an accommodation for a keyboard user, and the gap is worth owning deliberately rather than rediscovering.

FIX SHAPE (when it is worked): give the unscheduled cards and grid cells real semantics and keyboard operation -- focusable session cards, an explicit select-then-place interaction, an announced result. The same change makes the surface drivable by an accessibility-tree agent.

SIZE: large.

HISTORY: originally filed high/urgent-tonight on the operator's 2026-08-12 ruling, made on a framing this agent supplied -- that the gap was a scored broken promise. The operator challenged that framing; rechecking the rubric and the requirements register showed it did not hold. Downgraded to low/post-deadline the same day, with the accounting above recorded so the question does not get reopened from the judgement's defects[] entry alone.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, ai-agenda judgement, defects[1] (free QA, not a scored item).

data.body: Downgraded high -> low and reframed. The urgency I originally attached to this was mine, not the evidence's: keyboard/agent agenda placement is absent from the R1-R50 register and from the rubric, and only one of 98 scored items (AIA-03, cannot_judge) touches it -- that item also being blocked independently by a fixture typing issue. MRQ-135/136/137 are minutes each and sit on a judge's actual path; this is a large change that rescues at most one item. Recommend it stays behind them and lands after the deadline.

provenance.reason: Operator ruling 2026-08-12: revived as V2-1. Click-to-place unblocks four ai-agenda items including two cannot_judge; that is a different and stronger case than the keyboard-a11y framing this ticket was downgraded on.

data.to:
REVIVED AS V2-1 — CRITICAL, ~90 min. Operator ruling 2026-08-12. This ticket was downgraded to low/post-deadline earlier today and is now the single largest eval unlock left. Read the whole of this description: the reason it is back is NOT the reason it was filed.

WHY THE DOWNGRADE WAS RIGHT AND WHY IT NO LONGER APPLIES.
Filed originally as 'keyboard accessibility is a broken promise'. That framing did not survive checking: keyboard placement appears in NO rubric criterion and in NO requirement in the R1-R50 register, and only one scored item cited it. Downgraded on that evidence.
The V2 audit (Fable, surface:55) found the stronger case the original framing missed: the grid is UNDRIVABLE by a snapshot-driven harness, and undrivable means UNJUDGEABLE. That does not cost style points — it costs four items outright, two of them cannot_judge, which are excluded from the denominator and therefore make 100% unreachable while they stand.

WHAT IT CLOSES: AIA-03 (w3, cannot_judge), AIA-04 (w3, partial), AIA-05 (w2, partial), AIA-06 (w2, cannot_judge). Ten of ai-agenda's eighteen weight, from one change. It is the largest single unlock remaining on the board.

HUMAN PROBLEM. An organizer on a keyboard, a screen-reader user, and every agent Marquee claims as a first-class operator (PHILOSOPHY section 3, 'agent-native by design ... no privileged surface') cannot schedule a session. The grid is the product's centerpiece and it is mouse-only.

GOOD LOOKS LIKE — CLICK-TO-PLACE AS A PEER OF DRAG, NOT A REPLACEMENT:
- Activating an unscheduled card (click or Enter) arms it and announces 'Placing: {title}'.
- Every free time x room cell becomes a real button, labelled 'Place at 10:00 · Room 2A'.
- Activating one places through the SAME placement API the drop handler calls. Not a parallel path — the same one, so persistence, conflicts and audit all come for free.
- A placed tile offers 'Move...' (re-entering the same mode) and 'Unplace'.
- Escape disarms.
- No layout shift when arming: reserve the state line. DESIGN.md craft rule — elements never jump.

DRAG MUST KEEP WORKING. This is additive. Do not regress the mouse path.

VERIFY, KEYBOARD-ONLY: place an unscheduled session; reload (it persists); place a same-speaker overlap and watch the conflict panel gain the double-booking; move it clear and watch the conflict clear; unplace it. THEN once via an agent snapshot, confirming the accessibility tree exposes the cells as named buttons — that snapshot check is the whole point of the ticket, so do not skip it.

SEQUENCING — SAME FILE AS MRQ-148 (in flight). AgendaPage.tsx. Start after MRQ-148's PR is cut, or coordinate with that agent directly. Do not run two agents blind in the same file. MRQ-157 (15-minute increments) is third in this chain and composes with the 'Place at {time}' buttons this ticket creates.

Source: .briefs/eval-gap-v2-human-lens.md section 4, V2-1.

provenance.reason: Revived as V2-1 per operator ruling; re-scoped from keyboard-a11y framing to the judgeability unlock.

data.body: Revived as V2-1 and raised low -> critical, per operator ruling 2026-08-12, on evidence I did not have when I downgraded it. My downgrade was correct on its own terms — keyboard placement is in no rubric criterion and no requirement, and I verified that against the R1-R50 register. What I missed is that judgeability is not the same question as accessibility: a snapshot-driven harness cannot drive the grid at all, so AIA-03/04/05/06 cannot be scored, and two of those are cannot_judge, which blocks 100% outright. Ten of ai-agenda's eighteen weight turn on this one change. Scope is now click-to-place as a peer of drag, through the same placement API. Sequenced behind MRQ-148 (same file).

PR #145 is open.

Validation: full `npm run pr-gate -- --ticket MRQ-141` passed (931 tests, 39.6s). In the seeded local Worker, keyboard activation placed an unscheduled same-speaker session, reload preserved it, the conflict panel went 7 to 9 and showed the Beyang Liu double-booking, moving it clear returned the panel to 7 with that row gone, and Unplace returned it to the pool. The accessibility snapshot exposed `button "Place at 12:00 · Metropolitan Ballroom"`.

The c11 right-pane WebView was attempted but timed out under fleet load; the recorded browser flow used installed local Chrome against the same Worker and demo data.
